# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–5 (Complete and Final – Updated 65)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; now spring of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford; Also: Chiswick Mall (Miss Pinkerton's academy), Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, playground with tree and broken glass on wall, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Quenwick (harbor town), Wilhaven (harbor town), St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Cheltenham
- **Vauxhall Garden Details**: Majestic entrance with creaking vehicle, gilt cockle-shell staging, panorama of Moscow exhibit, bell for fireworks, dark walks with pasteboard Solitary hermit, supper boxes, musicians in gilt scallop-shell, lit garden with audience gathering capability
- **Recurring Environmental Details**: Rain threatening but holding off since morning; wind from water with salt and tar smell; gulls quarreling over fish heads by steps; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; frost silvering hedges overnight; light going early as spring approaches; children chasing hoop down lane; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; somewhere dog barked at nothing and then went quiet; river up again in spring; muddy square

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return to Middlemarch; now married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea's life acts not ideally beautiful but mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window; solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations; Fred remains steady, told Mary happiness half owing to Farebrother; never wholly free from misled hopefulness but gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner; three boys only, youngest resembles grandfather

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony; had dismal precocity of poverty
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; dressed in white with bare shoulders; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist; sings better than Amelia
- **Departure from Chiswick**: Threw Dixonary at Miss Jemima; obtained governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family after months-long battle to cancel indentures; Miss Pinkerton recommended her: "I cannot find fault with Miss Sharp's conduct except to myself; must allow her talents and accomplishments are of high order"
- **Strategy and Calculations**: Determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed since age eight when caught stealing jam by godmother; capable of calculated charm and intimacy; upon learning of Joseph Sedley's wealth and unmarried status, determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"
- **At Sedley Household and Romance Progress**: Invited by Amelia for week before governess duties; won over entire household through charming behavior; left alone with Joseph in drawing-room while Amelia and George went to piano; occupied knitting green silk purse; conversation established great confidence and intimacy; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music ended; Joseph continued presenting nosegays; Rebecca refused his request to sing, citing low spirits; asked him to help finish green silk purse; Joseph seated tete-a-tete looking at her with killing expression, hands bound in web of green silk; Joseph lay awake thinking of marrying her, concluded "It's evident the poor devil's in love with me"; thought "I might go farther, and fare worse"; Osborne caught Miss Sharp's eye fixed keenly upon him, at which he blushed and Rebecca thought "Ah, mon beau Monsieur! I think I have YOUR gauge"
- **At Vauxhall**: Took Jos's arm as matter of course going to dinner; sat by him on box of his open carriage; everyone seemed to understand marriage was expected; Rebecca felt want of dear, tender mother to manage business and extract proposal; lost themselves in solitary walk with Joseph among five score other couples; situation felt extremely tender and critical; at panorama of Moscow, rude fellow treading on her foot caused her to fall back with shriek into Joseph's arms, increasing his tenderness; Joseph told her several favorite Indian stories again (sixth time); Joseph said "SHOULD you?" with most killing tenderness and was about to ask tender question (could feel feverish pulsations of his heart against her hand near it) when bell rang for fireworks; later in supper box during Joseph's inebriation, when Jos clasped her round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling," Rebecca started but could not get away her hand; laughter outside redoubled
- **After Vauxhall**: Spent day after Vauxhall in observation from little bed-room on second floor watching for Joseph's arrival; began feeling distrust and hatred toward George Osborne after he laughed and bantered her with liveliness about her effect on Jos; feared Osborne had frightened Joseph away; heart beat quite quick; told Osborne "there's nobody to defend ME"; never spoke word to Amelia about Joseph that evening; Jos never came all that day

**Joseph Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Position and Background**: In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint and returned to Europe; does not live with family but has own lodgings like gay young bachelor
- **Appearance and Habits**: Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres, appears at opera; extremely talkative in man's society; told several tiger-hunting stories including one about Miss Cutler and Lance the surgeon
- **Vauxhall Behavior**: Escorted Rebecca to dinner and through gardens; at supper, was in his glory ordering waiters about with great majesty; made the salad; uncorked Champagne; carved chickens; ate and drank greater part of refreshments; insisted upon bowl of rack punch; drank up entire contents of bowl; became increasingly lively, talked and laughed so loud as to bring scores of listeners round the box; volunteered to sing in maudlin high key, almost drew away audience from musicians, received great applause; became as bold as a lion, clasped Rebecca round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; continued to drink, make love, and sing; winked and waved glass gracefully to audience; challenged all or any to come in and take share of punch
- **Critical Event - Vauxhall Aftermath**: George Osborne rose to interfere with commotion; single push from Osborne's finger sent Jos puffing back into seat; Osborne removed ladies in safety; Jos kissed hand to retreating ladies hiccupping "Bless you! Bless you!"; seized Dobbin's hand weeping pitiful way, confided secret of his loves, said he adored Rebecca, broken her heart, would marry her next morning at St. George's Hanover Square, would knock up Archbishop of Canterbury at Lambeth; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave gardens and hastened him to Lambeth Palace; once out of gates, Dobbin conveyed Jos into hackney-coach depositing him safely at his lodgings
- **Next Morning - Severe Hangover**: Jos groaning in agonies that morning Rebecca thought was to dawn upon her fortune; soda-water not invented yet; small beer only drink with which unhappy gentlemen soothed fever of previous night's potation; George Osborne found ex-Collector of Boggley Wollah groaning on sofa at his lodgings; Dobbin already in room good-naturedly tending patient of night before; two officers exchanged frightful sympathetic grins; Jos's valet Mr. Brush whispered to Osborne "Mr. Sedley was uncommon wild last night, sir...He wanted to fight the 'ackney-coachman, sir. The Capting was obliged to bring him upstairs in his harms like a babby"
- **Osborne's Mockery and Jos's Response to Ridicule**: Osborne pursued advantage pitilessly, thought Jos milksop, had been revolving marriage question pending between Jos and Rebecca in mind, was not over well pleased that member of family into which he was going to marry should make mesalliance with little nobody—little upstart governess; Osborne mocked Jos relentlessly saying he was maudlin, couldn't stand, made everybody laugh in Gardens, called Rebecca "your dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; ruthless young fellow seized Dobbin's hand and acted over scene to horror of original performer despite Dobbin's entreaties; when they quitted invalid leaving him under Doctor Gollop's hands, Osborne told Dobbin he had no right to give himself patronizing airs and make fools of them at Vauxhall; called Rebecca little schoolgirl ogling and making love to Jos; said family low enough already without her; said governess is all very well but he'd rather have lady for sister-in-law; said he is liberal man but has proper pride and knows his own station; said "let her know hers"; said he would take down great hectoring Nabob and prevent him being made greater fool; said that's why he told Jos to look out lest she brought action against him
- **Current Situation - Letter Sent**: Day after morning after Vauxhall, Jos sent letter to Amelia saying: "Dear Amelia,--I send you the 'Orphan of the Forest.' I was too ill to come yesterday. I leave town to-day for Cheltenham. Pray excuse me, if you can, to the amiable Miss Sharp, for my conduct at Vauxhall, and entreat her to pardon and forget every word I may have uttered when excited by that fatal supper. As soon as I have recovered, for my health is very much shaken, I shall go to Scotland for some months, and am"; thus avoided formal proposal entirely and quit town, leaving Rebecca's hopes dashed and Osborne's social interference effective
- **Father's Opinion**: Old Mr. Sedley has feeling akin to contempt for son; says Joseph is vain, selfish, lazy, effeminate; cannot endure his airs; will leave him half his property besides Joseph's own; sure Joseph would say "Good Gad!" and eat dinner as usual if family died; not anxious about him; says "Let him marry whom he likes. It's no affair of mine"
- **Narrative Significance**: Bowl of rack punch described as cause of all this history; punch influenced fates of all principal characters although most did not taste drop; young ladies did not drink it; Osborne did not like it; consequence of Jos drinking entire bowl was his inebriation and subsequent behavior; through lapse of twenty years narrator remembers consequence of two glasses; Jos had liver complaint and swallowed at least quart of abominable mixture

**Miss Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Character**: Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister; natural infirmity of tears; match-maker at heart; too good, too kind, doesn't know the world; innocent of rack punch's effects
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with George Osborne at single instant when he asked her for music
- **Regarding Rebecca and Vauxhall Aftermath**: Discovered million of virtues in Rebecca; warmed into most tender friendship; shows her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl; entirely agrees with mother's changed opinion regarding Joseph's choice; thought morning after Vauxhall that Jos must propose to-morrow; thought of dress as bridesmaid and presents for nice little sister-in-law and subsequent ceremony in which she might play principal part; actually sent away page Mr. Sambo's aide-de-camp to Jos's lodgings to ask for book he had promised and how he was; reply through Jos's man Mr. Brush was that his master was ill in bed and just had doctor with him; believed he must come to-morrow but never had courage to speak word on subject to Rebecca; looked reprovingly at George when he laughed at Rebecca; told him he was too kind, doesn't know the world; after Jos left town, never had further word from him
- **At Vauxhall**: George took charge of her; looked as happy as rose-tree in sunshine; at supper, was in mated pair with George, prattling away quite happily

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; received silver cup at six weeks old; received coral with gold whistle and bells at six months; regularly "tipped" at Christmas; thrashed by Joseph Sedley when hobbadehoy
- **Character and Feelings**: Clever artist; felt extraordinary, almost irresistible impulse to seize Amelia in arms and kiss her; hinted he should like to sit in dark during piano performance; somehow already present at Russell Square when Joseph arrived next morning
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying Amelia; banns read in respective families for ten years
- **At Vauxhall and Critical Intervention**: Asked Dobbin to look to shawls and things; paired off with Miss Sedley; at supper box with Amelia in mated pair; did not like rack punch; on point of knocking down gentleman in top-boots who proposed to take advantage of Jos's invitation when Dobbin intervened; rose to interfere with Jos; single push from his finger sent Jos puffing back into seat; removed ladies in safety
- **Post-Vauxhall Behavior and Campaign Against Rebecca-Jos Match**: Found Jos groaning on sofa next morning; had been revolving in mind marriage question pending between Jos and Rebecca and was not over well pleased that member of family into which he was going to marry should make mesalliance with little nobody—little upstart governess; pursued advantage pitilessly; thought Jos milksop; mocked Jos relentlessly about his behavior and romantic declarations; when Amelia came downstairs, bantered Rebecca with great liveliness upon effect of her charms on fat civilian; told her "Very good, Miss Sharp, I'll tell him"; inspired feeling of distrust and hatred in Rebecca; laughed at her piteous and discomfited mien; persisted in thinking joke most diverting one; when Rebecca came downstairs, continued liveliness and banter; when speaking to Amelia afterward, insisted Rebecca must learn her station, called her little friend, said she is helpless creature; told Amelia "you are too good--too kind. You don't know the world. I do. And your little friend Miss Sharp must learn her station"; acted over scene of Jos's maudlin behavior so drolly that Emmy laughed too; expressed manly compunction for having inflicted unnecessary unkindness upon Rebecca; his mockery and interference effectively discouraged Jos from pursuing proposal and contributed to Jos's decision to leave town

**William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Son of merchant/grocer; father keeps shop "Figs & Rudge" on Thames Street, City
- **Rise in Social Standing**: Despised grocer became Alderman Dobbin; Alderman Dobbin was Colonel of City Light Horse burning with military ardour to resist French Invasion; Colonel Dobbin's corps reviewed by Sovereign and Duke of York; colonel and alderman knighted; his son entered army; young Osborne followed in same regiment; they served in West Indies and in Canada; their regiment just come home
- **School Experience**: Giant amongst boys at Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, downcast and stupefied appearance, dog's-eared primer, tight corduroys; incapable of acquiring Latin rudiments; continually "taken down" by small boys; mercilessly bullied by entire school; bore everything patiently, entirely dumb and miserable; called "Figs" as nickname of reproach
- **Defense of George Osborne and Famous Fight**: While reading Arabian Nights under tree, witnessed Cuff beating small boy; sprang up and cried "Hold off, Cuff; don't bully that child any more"; previously threatened Cuff with leaden inkstand; after that Cuff never meddled personally with Dobbin; young Osborne told Dobbin that Cuff was licking him for breaking milk bottle; Dobbin said "I'll give you the worst thrashing you ever had in your life"; fought thirteen rounds: Cuff initially scientific and contemptuous, floored Dobbin three times; Dobbin quivering and determined, being left-handed brought that arm into action hitting Cuff's left eye and nose; by round 6, as many fellows shouting "Go it, Figs" as "Go it, Cuff"; by round 12, Cuff all abroad, lost presence of mind; round 13 final, Cuff reeling and groggy, Dobbin put in left on nose and sent him down; all boys shouted for Figs; Doctor threatened to flog Dobbin; Cuff acknowledged fault, saved Dobbin from whipping
- **Character Change**: In consequence of victory, character rose prodigiously in estimation; name "Figs" became respectable and popular nickname; "Old Figs" grew to name of kindness and endearment
- **Current Status and Feelings**: Attachment of Dobbin to George Osborne warm and generous as when two were schoolboys; young Osborne wrote home describing fight, telling mother Dobbin licked Cuff, fight was about him, and since Dobbin fought for him she ought to buy Tea and Sugar at his father's
- **At Vauxhall and Critical Intervention**: Asked by George to look after shawls and things; carried Amelia's white cashmere shawl; paid at door for whole party; attended under gilt cockle-shell while Mrs. Salmon performed Battle of Borodino cantata; tried to hum tune and found he was humming tune which Amelia Sedley sang on stairs as she came down to dinner; felt the pull of this tune; paraded twice before supper box where united couples were met, but nobody took notice of him; realized he was as clean forgotten as if he had never existed; decided he would only be de trop; walked away from couples saying "I'd best go and talk to the hermit" and strolled off into dark walk at end of which lived pasteboard Solitary; found being alone at Vauxhall most dismal sport ever entered into by bachelor; later, while walking about gardens, stepped up to supper box in most agitated state when commotion seemed inevitable; shouldered off great number of crowd who vanished before his cocked hat and fierce appearance; entered box in agitated state; intervened with gentleman in top-boots who proposed to take advantage of Jos's invitation
- **Post-Vauxhall**: Jos seized Dobbin's hand weeping pitiful way and confided secret of his loves; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave gardens and hastened him to Lambeth Palace; once out of gates, Dobbin conveyed Jos into hackney-coach depositing him safely at his lodgings; next morning found Jos groaning on sofa; was already in room good-naturedly tending patient; exchanged frightful sympathetic grins with Osborne; entreated Osborne to have mercy when Osborne mercilessly mocked Jos; told Osborne "I think it's very cruel of you to laugh, George"
- **Hummed Tune Significance**: Found himself unconsciously humming Amelia's tune while attending concert; this detail of his emotional attachment to Amelia planted but not yet developed

## Minor Characters
- **Orlwood and Hollwood Families**: Various minor appearances; Jotho Corrett remarked on river being up; Daena Wexwood and Breena sorted old letters by candlelight; Jotho Corrett remarked on river always being up in spring; Thiena Hollwood only shrugged at rain question; Ridan Corrett read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints; Jotho took Ridette Lindson in marriage at Quenwick before spring was out; couple lived in Quenwick thereafter; Mazek Hollwood remarked "The price of salt is a scandal" and gave up idleness to work as shepherd; Aessa Hollwood walked long way round to avoid muddy square; Ulvie Hollwood answered "Will it rain, do you think?" with only a shrug, fell asleep in chair before fire had caught, mended torn sleeve by window and said little, walked long way round to avoid muddy square, swore to Mazek to carry sealed letter to Salford and shook on it
- **Lindson-Hollmere Blood Debt**: Late one night Fedette Orlwood confided to eldest daughter that Lindson family once owed blood debt to Hollmere family; Fedette told Fetho Hollmere
- **Other Characters**: Doctor Gollop (Jos's physician); Mr. Brush (Jos's valet—most solemn and correct gentleman with muteness and gravity of undertaker); Mr. Sambo (Sedley household page, aide-de-camp); Doctor Swishtail (seminary headmaster)

## Critical Events and Current Status
- **Vauxhall Evening (Spring of First Year)**: Planned excursion of young people; Jos escorted Rebecca, George escorted Amelia, Dobbin attended as extra; couples separated despite solemn promises to stay together; Rebecca and Jos nearly prompted proposal at panorama of Moscow, again at solitary walk; critical moment interrupted by fireworks bell; at supper, Jos drank entire bowl of rack punch, became inebriated and made public spectacle of himself, called Rebecca "my dearest diddle-diddle-darling," clasped her round waist; commotion involving gentleman in top-boots averted by Osborne and Dobbin; Jos confided marriage plans to weeping Dobbin who shrewdly removed him from gardens and conveyed him home
- **Morning After (Day Following Vauxhall)**: Jos incapacitated by severe hangover; George Osborne visited and mercilessly mocked Jos about his behavior; Osborne expressed displeasure at Jos's potential mesalliance with Rebecca, calling her governess and little nobody; Osborne's mockery and interference discouraged Jos from pursuing proposal; Amelia believed Jos would come to-morrow; Rebecca watched anxiously from bedroom window; Jos never appeared that day
- **Final Resolution - Jos Flees Town**: Jos sent letter to Amelia apologizing for Vauxhall conduct, attributing behavior to rack punch, announcing he was leaving town immediately for Cheltenham, saying health very much shaken, planning to go to Scotland for some months after recovery; thus formal proposal never occurred; Rebecca's calculated romantic scheme failed; Jos abandoned town avoiding both Rebecca and the social ridicule Osborne had inflicted
